title: sdk: bridge auth+retry refactor, add streaming iterators across Python/TS/Go, and bump SDK versions
author: Maya Patel
description:
Motivation and summary: This PR introduces a lightweight SDK bridge that consolidates auth token refresh and retry/backoff behavior used by the Python, TypeScript, and Go SDK packages. It also standardizes streaming ergonomics (Python generator, TS AsyncIterable, Go channel-based iterator) to provide parity across SDKs and makes small API surface tweaks to improve developer ergonomics. Finally, it bumps the SDK package versions to reflect the ergonomics and bug fixes.

What changed (high level):
- New shared runtime component: packages/sdk-bridge/auth-retry-shim implemented in the monorepo. The shim centralizes token refresh locking and jittered exponential backoff logic, removing duplicated implementations across SDKs.
- Streaming API parity: Python: StreamIterator (sync generator) exposed on Client.stream(); TypeScript: stream() now returns AsyncIterable<StreamChunk>; Go: Stream: returns a channel + error sentinel (StreamIterator). Each SDK maps to idiomatic patterns but shares the same underlying contract.
- Backwards-compatible adapters for existing consumers: wrappers included so older call sites keep working; documented migration notes in each package README.
- Tests: added cross-SDK conformance tests in test/integration/sdk-parity to validate token refresh under contention and streaming chunk ordering semantics.
- Version bumps: python 0.9.3 -> 0.10.0, typescript 1.4.2 -> 1.5.0, go 0.8.1 -> 0.9.0.

Checklist:
- [x] Implement bridge shim with clear public interface
- [x] Replace SDK-local auth/retry with bridge calls
- [x] Add streaming iterators and examples for each SDK
- [x] Add unit + integration tests for concurrency and streaming parity
- [x] Update changelogs and package versions
- [x] Run full CI and fix flakes

Commits summary:
- feat(bridge): add auth-retry-shim with token mutex and backoff policy
- refactor(python): route auth calls to bridge; add StreamIterator wrapper
- feat(ts): expose AsyncIterable stream, integrate bridge for auth/retries
- feat(go): introduce stream iterator channel + bridge client calls
- test(integration): add sdk-parity tests simulating token expiry and heavy concurrency
- docs(sdk): migration notes and examples for streaming usage
- chore: bump versions and update CHANGELOGs

Files changed (representative):
- packages/sdk-bridge/src/auth_retry_shim.ts
- sdks/python/redwood/bridge_client.py
- sdks/python/redwood/streaming.py
- sdks/typescript/packages/sdk/src/bridge.ts
- sdks/typescript/packages/sdk/src/stream.ts
- sdks/go/redwood/bridge.go
- sdks/go/redwood/stream_iterator.go
- test/integration/sdk-parity/test_token_race.py
- test/integration/sdk-parity/test_stream_ordering.ts
- docs/sdk/migrations/streaming.md

Developer notes / motivation:
Previously each SDK implemented its own token refresh locking and retry/backoff semantics which led to subtle differences and occasional production inconsistencies (double-refresh races under heavy concurrent requests, different jitter parameters). Centralizing this into a small bridge component reduces duplication, makes behavior auditable, and makes future changes (e.g. adaptive backoff) take effect across all SDKs with a single change. Streaming ergonomics were slightly divergent between SDKs and caused confusion in our docs and example apps; aligning the outward shape (generator/AsyncIterable/channel) while keeping idiomatic language bindings helps reduce onboarding friction.

Compatibility and migration:
- Existing call sites that used the older streaming helpers will receive deprecation warnings for one release; compatibility wrappers are included and tested.
- The bridge API is internal to the monorepo packages and not exported as a public top-level package; customers see only the SDK package bumps.

Testing and CI:
- Initial CI run had flaky test failures in test_stream_ordering.ts (race in mock transport). I pushed a fix that serializes chunk timestamps in the mock transport and retried CI. Final CI: all checks green (unit, lint, integration, e2e smoke).

Notes for reviewers:
- Pay attention to the token refresh locking in auth_retry_shim.ts (Mutex logic + prometheus counters). I tried to keep the lock window minimal to avoid blocking user requests.
- The StreamIterator design in Python intentionally yields bytes-like chunks; higher-level convenience wrappers are left to the examples directory.
- The TS AsyncIterable implementation avoids buffering an entire response and propagates errors via iterator.throw per standard semantics.

Release notes: 
- Consolidated token refresh + retry logic across SDKs (reduces duplicate refreshes under concurrency)
- Introduced consistent streaming ergonomics for Python (StreamIterator), TypeScript (AsyncIterable), and Go (channel iterator)
- Bumped SDK versions: python 0.10.0, typescript 1.5.0, go 0.9.0
- Backwards-compatible wrappers included; deprecation warnings added for old helpers
